overview.description: Responsible practice is now a hiring requirement: biosafety levels (BSL-1 to 4) protect people and environment, while biosecurity and dual-use (DURC) governance protect against misuse. Knowing containment, IBC approval, and synthesis screening is table stakes.
objectives: match work to the right biosafety level (BSL-1 to BSL-4)
apply containment, PPE, and waste/decontamination practices
understand dual-use research of concern (DURC) and responsible innovation
know that synthesized DNA is screened and why (biosecurity)

steps.description: Responsible practice is now a hiring requirement: biosafety levels (BSL-1 to 4) protect people and environment, while biosecurity and dual-use (DURC) governance protect against misuse. Knowing containment, IBC approval, and synthesis screening is table stakes.
steps.intro: Biosafety protects against accidents; biosecurity protects against misuse. Both are professional obligations - and increasingly, legal and funding requirements - not optional extras.

instructions.title: Assess the risk
instructions.description: Classify the agent and work; determine the required biosafety level and containment.

instructions.title: Contain & protect
instructions.description: Use the right facility, PPE, and validated decontamination/waste procedures for that BSL.

instructions.title: Get oversight
instructions.description: Route recombinant/dual-use work through the appropriate committee (IBC) and follow DURC policy.

instructions.title: Think biosecurity
instructions.description: Understand that gene-synthesis providers screen orders against pathogens/toxins, and design work responsibly from the start.

submission.description: Given a proposed experiment, assign the biosafety level and containment, and identify any dual-use/biosecurity concerns and the oversight it would require.
